Subject: PO vs Credit Card — procurement path & next steps (post-demo)

Hey James / Priya — thanks again for your time on the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- What we heard: Acme runs a centralized AP process for vendors; purchases above ~$25k typically go via PO + contract, smaller subscriptions can be put on a corporate card. You asked about marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace) as an alternative.
- Redwood commercial options that fit what we discussed: (A) Annual contract with PO & Net30 (recommended for Dedicated / reserved capacity), (B) Hosted API on card for quick start / POC (monthly recurring), (C) Marketplace listing if you need centralized procurement + consolidated billing.
- Asks for you: Can you confirm the threshold for PO vs card (amount, approval path), whether your legal requires any specific contract clauses (data handling, SOC 2), and whether AP requires vendor onboarding docs (W-9, COI, bank info) before issuing a PO?

I attached a one-page mutual action plan and a pricing options sheet to make it easier to pick a path. Proposed next steps: 
1) You confirm procurement preference (PO vs card vs marketplace) and list of vendor docs required.
2) If PO path, we’ll have legal/ops prepare a standard SOW and routing for Docusign and provide invoice instructions.
3) If card path, we can provision a short-term monthly seat to start the POC immediately.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with procurement if that helps.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (1 page), Redwood_Pricing_Options.xlsx (pricing tiers)

From: James Holloway <j.holloway@acme-energy.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: PO vs Credit Card — procurement path & next steps (post-demo)

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from my side: 

- AP policy: Anything over $25,000 needs a PO and goes through the central AP team for approval (roughly a 2–3 week lead time once we have signed paperwork). Purchases <$5,000 can be done on a corporate card. Between $5k–$25k is handled case-by-case and needs director approval.
- Vendor onboarding: We will need standard vendor docs (W-9, Certificate of Insurance, vendor contact, remit-to address) and proof of SOC 2 / security posture for hosting vendors.
- Marketplace: We could potentially purchase through AWS Marketplace, but that requires you to be listed and it may add an additional annual contract term. Marketplace simplifies internal approvals for us but can change pricing cadence.

For this opportunity, I think the most likely path is PO + contract if we go with Dedicated or a multi-month committed plan. For a short POC (1 month), card would be fine. Can Marissa/Aditya share a sample SOW and the vendor packet? Also can you confirm invoicing details (email to AP and remit-to)?

Thanks,
James
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Energy
j.holloway@acme-energy.com | +1 617-555-0987

James / Priya — thanks for the details and the quick turnaround. Sharing a couple of concrete options and attached docs so your AP/legal team can review: 

Option 1 — PO + Annual contract (recommended for Dedicated / reserved capacity):
- Commercial: Annual commitment, invoiced upfront or quarterly via PO, Standard Redwood Master Services Agreement + SOW.
- Payment terms: Net30 by default (can discuss Net45 for enterprise deals).
- Onboarding: We’ll provide SOC 2 report, W-9, COI, and vendor setup packet.

Option 2 — Card-based Hosted POC (fastest time-to-value):
- Commercial: Month-to-month subscription on corporate card, can convert to PO/contract later.
- Onboarding: Minimal — we can provision access right away.

Option 3 — AWS Marketplace (if you prefer procurement through marketplace):
- Commercial: Pricing may differ due to marketplace fees; consolidated billing to AWS account.
- Timing: Requires Redwood listing and Marketplace terms; can take extra lead time to enable.

Attached: Redwood_Pricing_Options.xlsx (tiered pricing + estimated usage), Redwood_Vendor_Onboarding_Packet.zip (W-9, COI template, SOC 2 attestation summary).

If PO is the path, we’ll: (1) send standard MSA + SOW for signature (Docusign), (2) generate invoice referencing your PO number and remit-to info, and (3) provision the environment once payment terms are met.

Aditya / Laura — I’ll coordinate with Sales Ops to confirm invoice remittance details and SOW template.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Estimated timeline from our side: we can obtain an internal PO in ~2 weeks after we receive signed documents and vendor packet. For the POC on card, we can spin up immediately.
